successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Arpad's lands, 'converted into two provinces' in 740 BC; 'Afterward Arpad served a provincial capital'

ledger.x: early 9th century BC: Gusi of Yakhan founds Bit Agusi.
c. 823 BC: Bit Agusi leads a local alliance and wins independence. Stage 3 (c. 823 BC): 'Bit Agusi leads a local alliance opposing Assyrian hegemony'.

c. 823 BC (bridged): Aram-Damascus' supremacy. The page's stage 4 has 'Aram-Damascus's supremacy' lasting 'until approximately 805 BC' with Hazael prominent; the page does not say the supremacy was over Bit Agusi itself, so this is a low-confidence reading of the stage list.
c. 805 BC: Damascus' supremacy ends. Stage 4 'lasts until approximately 805 BC'; stage 5 (c. 800 to 754 BC) sees Hamath and Luash 'arise in the south'.
754 BC (bridged): the Kingdom of Arpad takes Aleppo.
740 BC: the Kingdom of Arpad ends as an Assyrian province.

wars.name: Shalmaneser III's subjugation of Bit Agusi
wars.outcome: Arame submits in 858 BC; Bit Agusi is subjugated to Assyria in stage 2 (841-823 BC) and frees itself c.

wars.name: The coalition against Zakkur of Hamath
wars.outcome: 'Zakkur survived the siege' at Tell Afis; 'led by the king of Bit Agusi' and incited by Ben-Hadad III.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's siege of Arpad
wars.outcome: Three years of siege; Arpad conquered in 740 BC and its lands converted into two provinces.

certainty.note: The page gives only the maximum extent (A'zaz to Hamath); the Hamath border was a dispute settled by Assyria c.
